Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:10:1.hebrew: המרבה בפירות - המרבה שכר לעצמו בפירות. ובגמרא מפרש דבהלוואת כסף או פירות נמי הוי תרבית, שהרי מתרבה ממונו, והכא ריבית דרבנן קמפרש דרך מקח וממכר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:10:1.english: One who increases [profit] through produce - [This means] one who increases profit for himself through produce. And in the Gemara it explains that in a loan of money or produce it is also tarbit, since his money increases; and here [the Mishnah] is explaining rabbinic interest [occurring] by way of buying and selling.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:10:2.hebrew: דינר זהב - כ"ה דינר כסף:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:10:2.english: A gold dinar - [is worth] twenty-five silver dinars.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:10:3.hebrew: וכן השער - כך היו נמכרין בעיר, והותר לו לתת מעות עכשיו על מנת ליתן לו זה חטין כל ימות השנה בדמים הללו כשיעור מעותיו, ואף על פי שעכשיו אין לו חטין, דתנן בפירקין (עב ב): יצא השער, פוסקין, ואף על פי שאין לזה, יש לזה; ויכול המוכר הלז לקנותם עתה במעות הללו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:10:3.english: And such was the [market] price - That is how they were being sold in the city, and it was permitted for him to give money now on condition that this [seller] give him wheat throughout the year at this price, according to the amount of his money — even though he does not have wheat now — as we learned in a Mishnah in our chapter (72b): "[Once] the [market] price has gone out, one may fix [a price], and even though this one does not have [it], another has [it]," and this seller can buy them now with this money.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:10:4.english: Wheat stood - after a time, at thirty dinars.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:10:5.hebrew: אמר לו תן לי חטיי - וזו מותרת היא אם נתן לו חטין, אבל פסוק היין שפוסק לו לתת בהן אסור, הואיל ואין לו, שמא יוקיר היין, ואף על פי שפוסק עמו כשער היין של עכשיו וכבר יצא השער. ובגמרא מפרש טעמא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:10:5.english: He said to him, "Give me my wheat" - And this [initial transaction] is permitted if he gave him wheat, but the fixing [of the price] of the wine that he contracts with him to give in exchange for it is prohibited, since he does not have [wine in his possession], lest the wine appreciate [in value], even though he contracts with him at the current market price of wine and the market price has already been established. And in the Gemara, [it] explains the reason.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:12:1.hebrew: לרבית דאורייתא - דרך הלואה משמע, כדכתיב (משלי כ״ח:ח׳) מרבה הונו בנשך ובתרבית:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:12:1.english: Interest by Torah law - [This] refers to [interest] by way of a loan, as it is written (Proverbs 28:8): “He who increases his wealth by neshekh and by tarbit.”

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:12:2.hebrew: והכתיב נשך כסף ורבית אוכל - "את כספך לא תתן לו בנשך ובמרבית לא תתן אכלך", ומדחלקו לשני לאוין, תרתי נינהו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:12:2.english: And is it not written: neshekh [for] money and ribit [for] food - [As the verse states:] “You shall not give him your money with neshekh, and with marbit you shall not give your food” (Leviticus 25:37), and since [Scripture] divided it into two prohibitions, they are two [distinct matters].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:13:1.english: Is there neshekh - That one bites his fellow, yet his [own] money does not increase?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:13:2.english: And is there tarbit - That the lender profits and the borrower is not bitten.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:13:3.english: Neshekh without tarbit - How do we illustrate it?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:14:1.english: For example, where he lent - He lent him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:14:2.english: One hundred - perutot for one hundred and twenty.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:14:5.english: For a danka - For a silver ma'ah, which is one-sixth of a dinar.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:15:1.hebrew: אי בתר מעיקרא אזלת - אי חשבת להני פרוטות השתא כדמעיקרא, הרי נשך והרי תרבית, שהוא יכול ליקח בהם מעה במאה, ונשכר עשרים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:15:1.english: If you go according to the initial [value] - If you reckon these perutot now as [they were] initially, there is neshekh and there is tarbit, for he can buy with them a ma'ah for a hundred [perutot], and he profits twenty [perutot].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:15:2.hebrew: לא נשך איכא - שהלוה יכול לקנותם במעה, וזה שוה מעה הלוהו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:15:2.english: There is no neshekh - For the borrower can buy them for a ma'ah, and this [lender] lent him the value of a ma'ah.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:16:1.hebrew: בחומשא - יכול ליקח בהן כסף חומש דינר, שהוא יותר על שתות:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:16:1.english: For one-fifth [of a dinar] - One can purchase with them silver [worth] one-fifth of a dinar, which is more than one-sixth.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:19:1.hebrew: אין לי - שיהא עובר אלא על לאו של נשך בכסף, ועל לאו של ריבית באוכל. מנין שהוא עובר על הלוואת פירות אף משום לאו דנשך:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:19:1.english: I have - [derived] that one transgresses only the negative commandment of neshekh with money, and the negative commandment of ribit with food. From where [is it derived] that one transgresses regarding a loan of produce also on account of the negative commandment of neshekh?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:19:2.hebrew: תלמוד לומר - "לא תשיך לאחיך נשך אוכל". ומקרא זה בלוה נאמר, מדלא כתיב "לא תשוך לאחיך", והראשון נאמר במלוה, דכתיב לעיל מיניה "אל תקח מאתו וגו'". ומיהו שמעת מינה מיהא דשייך לשון נשך באוכל:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:19:2.english: The verse states - "You shall not cause your brother to take interest [tashikh] ... neshekh of food" [Deuteronomy 23:20]. Now, this verse is stated regarding the borrower — since it is not written "You shall not take interest from your brother" [tashokh] — whereas the first [verse] is stated regarding the lender, as it is written just before it: "Do not take from him, etc." [Leviticus 25:36]. Nevertheless, you learn from it at least that the term neshekh applies to food.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:19:3.english: From where [do we derive] ribit for money - [Meaning] that one also transgresses the second negative commandment of ribit.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:19:4.hebrew: ת"ל - בלוה, נשך כסף. אם אינו ענין לגופו לחייבו על לאו של נשך — שהרי כבר נאמר בראש המקרא לא תשיך, ובסופו נאמר כל דבר אשר ישך — תנהו ענין לרבית כסף. והשתא דשמעינן מלא תשיך בין כסף ובין אוכל, אייתרו תרוייהו — נשך כסף ונשך אוכל — לחייב את הלוה על לאו של רבית על שניהן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:19:4.english: The verse states - regarding the borrower, "neshekh of money." If it has no application to its own subject—to make him liable for the prohibition of neshekh, since it is already stated at the beginning of the verse, "You shall not pay interest [lo tashikh]," and at its end it is stated, "anything that is lent with interest [kol davar asher yishakh]"—apply it [instead] to ribit of money. And now that we derive from "lo tashikh" both money and food, both of them—"neshekh of money" and "neshekh of food"—are superfluous, [and serve] to make the borrower liable for the prohibition of ribit for both of them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:1:1.english: Because he eases the market rate - And hoarders of produce will see that [prices] have become cheaper and will sell cheaply.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:2:1.hebrew: מתיר בדבר הנראה - הלא יכול הלוקח לראות ולהבין מה דמי הפסולת הנברר מאלו שישנו באחרים, וטוב לו להעלות בדמיהן של אלו יתר על כן מפני הטורח:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:2:1.english: [He] permits [it] in a visible matter - Surely the buyer can see and understand what the value is of the waste sifted from these, which is [still] present in others, and it is worthwhile for him to pay more for these beyond that on account of the effort [saved].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:3:1.hebrew: משרבטין - לשון שרביט, כדמפרש לקמיה שזוקף שער הבהמה כשרביט, שתראה שמינה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:3:1.english: Stiffen [mesharbetin] - An expression of sharvit [a rod], as [the Gemara] explains below, that one makes the animal's hair stand erect like a rod so that it will appear fat.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:3:2.hebrew: ואין נופחין בקרביים - בני מעיים הנמכרים בבית הטבח, שיראו רחבים וגדולים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:3:2.english: And one may not inflate innards - Intestines that are sold in the butcher's shop, so that they appear wide and large.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:3:3.hebrew: ואין שורין בשר במים - שמלבין, והכחוש נראה שמן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:3:3.english: And one may not soak meat in water - For it turns white, and the lean [meat] appears fat.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:3:4.hebrew: מיא דחיזרא - משקין אותה מי סובין, והם נופחין מעיה ושערה נזקף:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:3:4.english: Bran water - They give [the animal] bran water to drink, and it inflates its innards and its hair stands on end.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:3:5.english: Mazkafta - Currying [the animal's hair], "estriller" in Old French.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:4:1.hebrew: למימרא תומי לסרבלא - פרנזי"ש. לייפותו, עושין לו תלאי מחוטי משי סביב:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:4:1.english: To put fringes on a cloak - *Franges* [in Old French, fringes]. To beautify it, they make for it an attachment of silk threads all around.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:4:2.english: To clean [lekaskosei] - [This means] enpresser [to press] in Old French, with bran water:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:4:3.english: Kirmei - Ornamented garments, ovrez [worked/embroidered] in Old French.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:4:4.english: To beat hemp garments - To beat hemp garments with wooden mallets so that their thread appears fine.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:4:5.english: To draw arrows - To paint arrows.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:4:7.hebrew: בחדתי - מותר, שאינו אלא ליפות, והרוצה להוסיף על דמיהם בשביל יופיים, מוחל הוא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:4:7.english: With new [ones] - [It is] permitted, for it is only to beautify [them], and one who wishes to add to their price because of their beauty waives [the extra cost].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:4:8.hebrew: בעתיקי - אסור, שגונב את העין, שנראים כחדשים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:4:8.english: With old [items] - [It is] prohibited, because it deceives the eye, as they appear like new.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:5:1.hebrew: צבעיה - שהיה זקנו לבן וצבעו שחור, ונראה כבחור:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:5:1.english: He dyed it - For his beard was white, and he dyed it black, and he appeared like a young man.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:5:2.hebrew: זיבנן - קנה אותי לעבד. ונכרי היה, דעבד עברי אסור לאחר חורבן, שאין היובל נוהג:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:5:2.english: Purchase me - Buy me as a slave. And he was a gentile, for [acquiring] a Hebrew slave is prohibited after the destruction [of the Temple], since the Jubilee [year] is not practiced.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:5:3.hebrew: ויהיו עניים בני ביתך - משנה היא (אבות פ"א מ"ה). טוב לי לפרנס עניי ישראל וישמשוני:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:5:3.english: And let the poor be members of your household - It is a Mishnah (Avot 1:5). It is better for me to support the poor of Israel and [have them] serve me.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:6:2.english: The righteous [person] is delivered from trouble - This [refers to] Rava.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:8:1.hebrew: איזהו נשך - שהוא נושך, דשקל מיניה מאי דלא יהיב ליה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 60b:8:1.english: Which is neshekh - [It is so called] because it bites, as he takes from him what he did not give him.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 60b:18:1.hebrew: למה חלקם הכתוב לעבור עליו בשני לאוין - וא"ת: ולמה שינה בלשון לכתוב "כספך לא תתן בנשך ובנשך לא תתן אכלך"? ויש לומר: כיון שהוצרך שני לאוין, אורחא דקרא לכתוב לשון משונה שהוא נאה יותר:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 60b:18:1.english: Why did the verse distinguish between them? To make him violate two prohibitions - And if you ask: Why did [Scripture] vary the phrasing to write, "Your money you shall not give at neshekh, and at neshekh [i.e., marbit] you shall not give your food"? One can answer: Since two prohibitions were needed, it is the manner of Scripture to write varied phrasing, as it is more elegant.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 60b:19:1.hebrew: נשך באוכל מנין - ואם תאמר: תחילה הוה ליה למדרש ריבית בכסף, דמפיק ליה מ"נשך כסף" הכתוב ברישא? ויש לומר: משום ד"נשך אוכל" כתיב בהדיא, וריבית כסף לא נפיק אלא ב"אם אינו ענין":
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 60b:19:1.english: "From where [is it derived that there is] neshekh with regard to food?" - And if you will say: first [the baraita] should have expounded ribit for money, since it derives it from "neshekh of money," which is written first [in the verse]? One can answer: [It expounds neshekh for food first] because "neshekh of food" is written explicitly, whereas ribit for money is only derived through [the principle of] "if it has no application [to its own matter]."

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 60b:8:1.hebrew: איזהו נשך. מאה בדנקא פרש"י - ק' פרוטות במעה, שהוא שתות דינר. וקשה: היאך הוזלו הפרוטו' כל כך? דבשער בינוני אין כי אם שנים ושלשים במעה; ומעה שני פונדיון, פונדיון ב' איסרים, איסר ח' פרוטות — היינו ל"ב פרוטות. ונראה כפירוש ריב"ן, דפירש ק' מעות בשתות מנה, שהוא ארבע סלעים וארבע מעות; א"נ ק' איסרים בשתות דינר זהב, שהוא ארבע דינרי כסף ומעה:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 60b:8:1.english: "Which is neshekh?" "One hundred for a danka," Rashi explained - [i.e.,] one hundred perutot for a ma'ah, which is a sixth of a dinar. And this is difficult: how did the perutot depreciate so much? For at the standard rate there are only thirty-two [perutot] in a ma'ah; a ma'ah is two pundi'onim, a pundi'on is two issars, [and] an issar is eight perutot — which is thirty-two perutot. And it appears [correct] like the explanation of Rivan, who explained [that it means] one hundred ma'ot for a sixth of a maneh, which is four sela'im and four ma'ot; or alternatively, one hundred issars for a sixth of a gold dinar, which is four silver dinars and a ma'ah.
